entries.english:
Co-plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Ursula Fuchs von Bimbach, née Romrod, acting as guardian of her minor son Hans Christoph Fuchs von und zu Bimbach.
Co-defendants/intervenors: Bishop Julius of Würzburg and Kilian Neudecker, the prince-bishop of Würzburg's centgrave at Oberschwarzach.
Plaintiff's attorney: Dr Sigismund Haffner (1613).
Defendant's attorney: Lic. Antonius Streitt (1593).
Contemporary subject: mandate for distraint, concerning the imprisonment of Christoph Wolf, the Fuchs Schultheiß at Ebersbrunn.
Modern subject: dispute over the jurisdiction of the cent court of Oberschwarzach at Ebersbrunn. During an armed incursion into Ebersbrunn, the co-defendant centgrave arrested the plaintiff's Schultheiß Christoph Wolf because he had wounded Michel Roeting, a subject of Ebrach at Ebersbrunn, in a brawl. Ursula Fuchs von Bimbach regarded this as an infringement of her Vogtei authority over her subjects at Ebersbrunn, which she said included punishing offenses. The defendant bishop maintained that the jurisdiction of the cent court at Oberschwarzach was not limited to serious criminal cases but covered all other cent cases as well, especially bodily injury.
Proceedings: Imperial Chamber Court, 1615–1616 (1615–1617).

Included: oath of lay judges for the Würzburg cent courts (item 5); Michel Roeting's testimony before the cent court at Oberschwarzach (item 6); the obligation of Fuchs's subjects at Ebersbrunn to render hereditary homage (item 8); a 1588 settlement before Margrave Georg Friedrich of Brandenburg-Ansbach and Brandenburg-Kulmbach concerning lordship of the village of Ebersbrunn, between Abbot Leonhard of Ebrach, the brothers Rudolf, Christoph, and Hans Sigmund Fuchs von Bimbach, and the tax collector, mayors, and council of Prichsenstadt acting for that town's hospital (item 10); and the 1614 revocation, by Fuchs's subjects Klaus Krebser and Stoffel Linck of Ebersbrunn, of the oath of allegiance they had rendered to the co-defendant centgrave out of fear (item 11).

The 1613 Würzburg commission register in the case of Wolf Jakob, Count of Schwarzenberg, against the Bishopric of Würzburg concerning two annual fairs at Markt Bibart (see order no. 1565) includes (item 14): King Friedrich III's 1442 order to all prelates, counts, knights, and men-at-arms of the Bishopric of Würzburg to render homage to the administrator Gottfried Schenk von Limpurg, authenticated by Abbot Karl II of St Burkard and Abbot Berthold of St Stephan in Würzburg in 1442; and a 1442 letter from several counts, lords, knights, and men-at-arms of the Bishopric of Würzburg to the mayor and council of Würzburg (nos. 6–7). It also includes extracts from agreements made by Bishops Johann II, Johann III, Rudolf II, and Konrad II with the knighthood and towns of the bishopric in 1412, 1456, 1467, and 1525, with Emperor Karl V's confirmation of the 1525 agreement in 1526 (nos. 8–11); the 1485 agreement between Michael and Siegmund von Schwarzenberg and Bishop Rudolf II of Würzburg concerning Stephansberg (no. 12); Count Wolfgang of Hohenlohe's 1535 invitation to Bishop Konrad II to attend a wedding (no. 13); and extracts of letters to Bishop Rudolf II of Würzburg, acknowledging his status as territorial lord, from the brothers Berthold, Elector of Mainz; Friedrich; Georg, Teutonic Order commander at Mergentheim; Heinrich, canon of Strasbourg; and Otto, Count of Henneberg-Aschach; as well as from the widowed Countess Margaretha of Henneberg-Aschach, née Duchess of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel (nos. 14–17).

A volume of exhibits from the same case (item 15) contains: an extract from a charter of Bishop Johann III concerning the dispute over Michael von Schwarzenberg's remarriage to Ursula Frankengrüner and his testamentary disposition made before Abbot Mauritius III of Würzburg's Scottish monastery, acting as papal commissioner, in 1458 (exhibit A); a judgment of the Imperial District Court of the Duchy of Franconia in the dispute between Philipp von Weinsberg and Reinhard Truchseß von Baldersheim over the reversion of fiefs at Unterbalbach, Reichelsburg (called Regelsberg in the file), and Burgerroth in 1477 (exhibit B); an extract from the judgment of Elector Ernst and Duke Albrecht of Saxony, acting as imperial commissioners, in the 1483 dispute between Bishop Rudolf II of Würzburg and Count Friedrich of Henneberg-Aschach, together with the Schultheiß, village headmen, and community of Linden (exhibit C); the 1500 settlement before Albrecht von Bibra, canon of Bamberg and Würzburg and provost of St Johann's monastery at Neumünster, and Bartholomäus von Herbilstadt, acting as arbiters, in the dispute between Bishop Rudolf II of Würzburg and Heinrich and Valentin von Bibra over redemption of the prince-bishop's share in Irmelshausen (exhibit D); Christoph Fuchs (von Bimbach), marshal and Amtmann at Zabelstein for the prince-bishop of Würzburg, issued an instrument of acknowledgment in 1481 concerning acceptance of Götz von Füllbach as a prince-bishop's servant (exhibit E); an extract from Bishop Rudolf II of Würzburg and Count Otto of Henneberg-Aschach's 1489 order concerning action against Hermann the Elder and Hermann the Younger Riedesel after they had declared a feud (exhibit F); Lorenz von Rosenberg's 1550 letters to Bishop Melchior of Würzburg concerning Joachim von Niedeck's suit before the Imperial Chamber Court, and the related Imperial Chamber Court judgment of 1551 (exhibits G–I and M); and Hans Eucharius von Rosenberg's 1574 letter to the defendant bishop concerning Zaisolph von Rosenberg's suit before the Imperial Chamber Court (see order no. 10946; exhibit K).

Also included are: Emperor Karl V's 1545 confirmation of King Karl IV's 1347 privilege concerning the Imperial District Court of the Duchy of Franconia (item 16); Emperor Karl IV's 1372 letter of enfeoffment to Bishop Gerhard of Würzburg concerning investiture with temporalities (item 17); Emperor Rudolf II's 1609 privilege against arrest for the Franconian Imperial Knighthood (item 18); and exhibits to the Würzburg submission brief, submitted on 11 April 1617: extracts from Imperial District Court registers concerning cases involving the knighthood, for 1499–1534, 1550–1554, 1560–1563, and 1570–1573, with annual lists of district judges and assessors (no. 8); a list of references in the Imperial District Court registers concerning Ebersbrunn, 1537–1581 (no. 9); and a printed 1534 privilege of Emperor Karl V for Bishop Konrad II protecting Würzburg privileges against acquisition by prescription and lapse through time in connection with the Reformation (no. 10).

Register: case began in 1615.
